items.title: PVC Pipes Swept Away by Helene Still Dominate Cleanup of NC River
items.original_title: PVC Pipes Swept Away by Helene Still Dominate Cleanup of NC River
items.rss_title: PVC Pipes Swept Away by Helene Still Dominate Cleanup of NC River
items.rss_description: They’re piled on river banks, lodged in uprooted trees, embedded in sediment and jammed under logs. Many are tangled in mounds of debris up to two stories high. Two years after Hurricane Helene leveled forests, bulldozed houses and filled western …
items.extracted_text: PVC Pipes Swept Away by Helene Still Dominate Cleanup of NC River Article 0 Comments They’re piled on river banks, lodged in uprooted trees, embedded in sediment and jammed under logs. Many are tangled in mounds of debris up to two stories high. Two years after Hurricane Helene leveled forests, bulldozed houses and filled western North Carolina rivers with everything from cars to refrigerators, the work of cleaning up the debris goes on. Along the iconic French Broad River, known for its whitewater rapids, one item stands out from the rest: massive numbers of PVC pipes that washed away from a factory north of Asheville. As Hurricane Isaias , the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, intensifies, the PVC pipes are a reminder that damage can disrupt lives for years after a storm passes. “Just the amount of time and energy that we put into removing all this pipe is exhausting,” said Jon Stamper, operations director at MountainTrue, the nonprofit conducting cleanup on several rivers affected by Helene. “We still have stretches of river that haven’t been touched.” MountainTrue estimates its crews have pulled hundreds of thousands of pipes from the river — most of which went to landfills — with an untold number still littering the river for 70 miles (113 kilometers) to a large lake at the Tennessee border. Canada-based IPEX would not say how many pipes were stored at its Woodfin, North Carolina, site before the storm or share results of a company-funded study of how much remains in the river, calling the information “commercially sensitive.” Officials said 60% of pipes stored outdoors at the site, sandwiched between railroad tracks and the river, were swept away by the 2024 flood, but most were recovered fairly quickly. The company acknowledged that the remaining debris is significant and has agreed to pay MountainTrue $500,000 toward continued cleanup on the French Broad, allowing the organization to continue working into next year. A $10 million state grant awarded to MountainTrue in 2025 to clean up debris in several western North Carolina rivers that was set to expire in December has been extended to February. The organization said there’s still a long way to go and estimates it has spent 50,000 work-hours and over $1.5 million on pipe removal, which is only in the French Broad. PVC pipe comprises 80% of the debris in some areas, according to MountainTrue, posing risks to rafters and kayakers, changing water flow and altering the ecosystem. “We understand the ongoing challenge,” IPEX CEO Colleen Pritchett said. “We recognize that … recovery efforts are complex, they’re resource-intensive, and it’s constantly shaped by the river conditions.” The Epic Flood Took Everyone by Surprise Hurricane Helene hit western North Carolina in late September 2024, dumping more than 30 inches (76 centimeters) of rain in some areas, triggering landslides, toppling trees, pushing buildings off their foundations and choking waterways. At IPEX, an earthen berm was the only thing separating tall stacks of pipes from the French Broad River. Company officials said they expected a so-called 100-year flood — meaning it has a 1% chance of occurring in any given year — and moved pipes out of that flood zone. But the flooding from Helene was 10 times worse. “We secured the site as best we could, and we sent people home a day before the flooding was expected,” said Johnny Drummond, vice president of manufacturing. He said the company did not anticipate a 1,000-year flood, which has a 1-in-1,000 chance of occurring. The company closed the factory for a couple of months afterward, with losses “well over $100 million,” Pritchett said. It has since invested over $100 million to repair and strengthen the buildings, and now is studying ways to contain the pipes in future floods — something MountainTrue publicly urged for months. Though there’s much more than IPEX debris still in the waterways, the pipes are so ubiquitous that “there are places where you go that it makes up almost everything that we remove,” said Stamper, who formerly worked for a whitewater river outfitter and now oversees 10 cleanup crews totaling about 100 people — many of them former river or fishing guides who lost their livelihoods after the hurricane. Removing the pipe is especially vexing because it binds with other debris and has become embedded in the river bottom, with fish and other creatures taking up residence inside. Stamper said he also worries about long-term environmental and health effects from the pipe, which can degrade and become brittle, leaving microplastics in the river. “We want to avoid that stuff sitting there forever and just slowly deteriorating and breaking into smaller and smaller pieces,” Stamper said. “Some of the pipe that’s been sitting out since Hurricane Helene that has been exposed to the sun all the time is getting to the point where you could crack it when you grab it.” Removing pipes is tedious, sometimes dangerous Some of the pipes — both straight, rigid plastic and flexible coils that have unraveled — are under huge piles of tangled logs topped by other debris, often in mounds 20 feet (6 meters) high. Cleanup crews “just sort of picture it as a jungle gym” that they must climb and balance on as they clear the pile, said Jemima Filiss-Cook, who leads the cleanup in Madison County, where most of the pipe is concentrated. She said many crew members were already cleaning up the river before MountainTrue hired them, as a way of “trauma bonding” over what had happened. They include avid outdoorspeople, including rock climbers, because the cleanup is “quite a tedious and technical process” that requires comfort with the job’s rigors, said Anna Alsobrook, MountainTrue’s French Broad Riverkeeper. Crews saw longer pipes into smaller chunks and load them on a boat, which is taken downstream to a landing spot and loaded onto a truck. Almost all of the pipes go to a landfill, though some in good condition are given to community members because there are no good recycling options, MountainTrue said. “I truly don’t think anybody else could do this work except for our debris team members,” Alsobrook said, noting they must be able to navigate whitewater rapids with a boat full of pipes and saws. The first priority was removing pipes that could pose an immediate danger or entrapment hazard to tubers or kayakers, and much of the remaining debris stranded in flood plains and on banks, especially around riverbends and corners, and vulnerable to being washed away in another flood, Stamper said. It becomes apparent many pipes are still in the river whenever water levels change, he said. MountainTrue is applying for other grants to help extend its program after state and IPEX funding run out, Stamper said, because it could take years to remove all the debris. “We’re going to do our best as long as the funding allows,” he said. “But there’s going to be pipe out there that we can’t get ever.” ___ Webber reported from Fenton, Michigan. items.title: Trump’s Executive Order on Dyed Diesel Provides Little Relief for Farmers and Truckers
items.original_title: Trump’s Executive Order on Dyed Diesel Provides Little Relief for Farmers and Truckers
items.rss_title: Trump’s Executive Order on Dyed Diesel Provides Little Relief for Farmers and Truckers
items.rss_description: Farmers, truckers and economists say a move to cut taxes on diesel will provide little relief from record-high fuel prices that have soared since the U.S. attacked Iran months ago. Industry groups said they appreciate President Donald Trump’s executive order …
items.extracted_text: Trump’s Executive Order on Dyed Diesel Provides Little Relief for Farmers and Truckers Article 1 Comment Farmers, truckers and economists say a move to cut taxes on diesel will provide little relief from record-high fuel prices that have soared since the U.S. attacked Iran months ago. Industry groups said they appreciate President Donald Trump’s executive order expanding the use of a diesel now reserved for off-road work, but farmers already have access to the fuel and many have already wrapped up harvest. Truckers will struggle to navigate differing state rules. “In the context of diesel prices that are over two dollars more than they were last year, it just doesn’t come close to closing that wound,” said Matt Perdue, president of the North Dakota Farmers Union. With less than a month to go before the November election , diesel prices continue to hit record highs as some farmers transport their crops for processing and others rush to complete their fall harvest. Many have been feeling the squeeze as costs for inputs like diesel, fertilizer and seed have soared thanks to refinery constraints and supply disruptions amid the Iran war. Diesel averaged $6.30 per gallon across the country on Wednesday, more than 70% higher than one year ago, according to motor club AAA. The executive order defers the $0.24 federal tax per gallon of regular diesel, used for road projects, until the end of the year. Most states also levy their own tax on diesel. “Dyed” diesel is the same as regular diesel, except for its red dye to help law enforcement enforce penalties for on-road use. It’s already allowed for off-road purposes like farming equipment, such as tractors and combines, as well as construction and heating uses. Who will see benefits Savings can compound if states take similar actions many have eased restrictions or waived taxes on dyed diesel, including South Dakota and Iowa. Perdue said North Dakota has waived the tax on regular diesel. But where the state decision is focused on farmers, he believes the federal decision would largely benefit those on other levels of the supply chain. Farmers who will see the most benefit are those who haul their own product, like livestock or fresh produce, on public roads. Those who have already wrapped up harvesting won’t see savings. “Most of our diesel use is behind us,” said Perdue, who grows spring wheat, durum and canola on his family farm. Both trucking companies and independent truckers may not see much relief either. The effect is likely to be negligible for big trucking companies because the order is on a federal level and states make their own rules, Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, wrote in a social media post. “The largest diesel users are the least likely to use dyed diesel,” he wrote. “A national carrier crossing five or six states in a day faces enormous risk with a patchwork of rules, legal in one state, and subject to fines in the next.” Many states exempt road diesel from sales tax but apply sales tax to dyed diesel instead, he said. Easing limits on red-dyed diesel will likely have a minimal effect for small truckers, who pay for fuel up front, said Todd Spencer, president and CEO of trade group the Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association. He estimates every $1 increase per gallon in fuel costs independent truckers about $400 more per week. Increased demand for dyed diesel The savings will be small, but it could still increase competition for dyed diesel, said David Ortega, food economics and policy professor at Michigan State University. “I think there’s a real chance this could backfire and make the situation worse for farmers,” he said. “Basically anybody that’s running a truck on the highway on regular diesel can now be using this off-highway diesel. Even someone that owns a diesel pickup truck potentially has access to this other type of diesel.” Perdue in North Dakota said he expects a “rush for dyed diesel, and we’ll see how the supply responds.” But not all dyed diesel pump stations are set up for larger trucks like semis, said Paul Mitchell, a professor of agricultural and applied economics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. “It’s going to come down to infrastructure ability to get your vehicles to a place that you can use and fill them up with,” he said. Supply shortages persist Henry Hanscom, American Trucking Associations chief advocacy and public affairs officer, pointed out that the executive order directs temporary penalty relief and potential tax deferral for using red-dyed diesel, not outright tax forgiveness. He said the ATA would review the Internal Revenue Service’s implementing guidance of the policy when it is available. Last month, Trump had threatened a diesel export ban, though he later said it is off the table. On Friday, G7 countries agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products. “One of the problems we have right now in the world is there’s not enough diesel fuel,” said Gregg Ibendahl, farm management specialist at Kansas State University. But underlying causes like geopolitical issues won’t be solved overnight. “The problem we’ve accumulated right now with the Strait of Hormuz and the Russia-Ukraine war, those are going to be longer term things to get fixed,” he said. “Getting that world supply back up again is going to be, I think, at least a year, even in the best cases.” ___ Anderson reported from New York. items.extracted_text: Tesla Drops ‘Self-Driving’ Branding to Appease Europe Regulators Article 0 Comments Tesla Inc. is backing away from its Full Self-Driving branding to help secure approval for the driver-assistance system in Europe, distancing the company from a name that has drawn criticism as dangerously misleading. The automaker has begun using the name “Tesla Assisted Driving” on its European websites in recent days. The US version of the same site is continuing to use “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” for the technology. Related: Tesla Is Browbeating The EU to OK Its Full Self-Driving Tech. The Pressure Is Working Tesla’s driver-assistance branding has long been a point of contention with regulators, safety advocates and even some Tesla customers, who say the name gives the impression of full autonomy even though drivers must still be alert and ready to take control of their vehicles. Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk has also been faulted by critics for pushing overly aggressive or unfounded claims about Tesla vehicles’ capabilities. The California Department of Motor Vehicles last year threatened to suspend Tesla’s sales in the state over allegedly misleading marketing of driver-assistance technology. Authorities backed down after the company took “corrective action,” including phasing out its Autopilot branding and specifying when Full Self-Driving — also known as FSD — must have driver supervision. FSD is a significant financial driver for Tesla’s automotive business, which typically charges drivers $99 a month for the system. It’s also key to Musk’s efforts to refashion the carmaker as a tech-forward company pioneering autonomous vehicles and robotics. Tesla is now seeking to bring the FSD system to Europe, which has been slow to embrace the technology. When Dutch regulators in April approved FSD, they emphasized that it was a more restrictive version than what is used in the US and said in a statement that “a vehicle with FSD Supervised is not self-driving.” The company continues to seek approval in other countries across the continent. items.title: Carpenter’s heart attack after restraining donkey ruled compensable
items.original_title: Carpenter’s heart attack after restraining donkey ruled compensable
items.rss_title: Carpenter’s heart attack after restraining donkey ruled compensable
items.rss_description: A New York appeals court on Thursday upheld workers compensation coverage for a carpenter who suffered a heart attack after helping restrain a donkey at his employer’s owner’s residence.
items.extracted_text: Gerard Mulligan, a carpenter for Moy Construction, was assigned to work on an animal shed when the owner’s spouse, also the company’s vice president, asked him to help return a loose donkey to the structure. Mr. Mulligan subsequently experienced chest pain, lightheadedness, and vomiting and sought benefits for a heart attack he attributed to physical strain at work, according to Matter of Mulligan v. Moy Construction Corp. , decided by the Appellate Division, Third Department. A workers compensation judge found that the employer and its insurer missed the deadline to contest the claim but denied benefits, concluding that Mr. Mulligan had not established a work-related injury and noting the absence of emergency room records. The Workers’ Compensation Board reviewed the records in the case file and established the claim. The appeals court affirmed, finding sufficient unrebutted medical evidence connecting the heart attack to Mr. Mulligan’s work. He testified that he exerted himself while preventing the donkey from escaping again, and his treating physician linked the heart attack to that exertion. The court said the insurer’s late filing barred it from offering testimony disputing causation, although Mr. Mulligan still had to establish the connection through medical evidence. The court declined to consider the insurer’s separate argument that its policy did not cover Mr. Mulligan because it had not raised that issue before the compensation judge or board. items.extracted_text: S.M.A.R.T. 2026 - Dans un monde qui change, les choix d'aujourd'hui façonneront les équilibres de demain. - France Assureurs Événement organisé sous le haut patronage de Monsieur Emmanuel MACRON, Président de la République. Climat, santé, démographie, territoires, cybersécurité : les mutations qui transforment nos sociétés s’accélèrent et redessinent nos modèles économiques, sociaux et politiques. Fidèles à leur rôle d’anticipation, les assureurs sont des observateurs de premier plan de ces évolutions. Ils en mesurent les impacts et développent, pour les particuliers, les entreprises et les territoires, des solutions en faveur d’une société plus résiliente. Organisé par France Assureurs, S.M.A.R.T. est le rendez-vous des décideurs, experts et acteurs engagés dans la réflexion et l’action face aux grands défis de notre temps. Cette année, S.M.A.R.T. se donne une ambition : choisir l’avenir en conjuguant vision et solutions . Vision, pour mieux comprendre les transformations à l’œuvre et ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives. Solutions, pour mettre en lumière les initiatives, innovations et leviers d’action qui permettront de les accompagner. Au programme Des interventions de personnalités françaises et européennes de premier plan Des débats consacrés aux grands enjeux climatiques, technologiques, démographiques, économiques et géopolitiques Des retours d’expérience et des solutions concrètes portées par des acteurs de terrain Une galerie de l’innovation mettant à l’honneur des initiatives inspirantes Des temps d’échange Un temps fort dédié à la jeunesse à travers le Challenge étudiant destiné à faire émerger de nouveaux regards sur les risques, les transitions et les métiers de l’assurance Si vous souhaitez avoir des informations ou participer à l’événement, merci de nous contacter à smart@franceassureurs.fr (Re)vivez les précédentes éditions de S.M.A.R.T. items.extracted_text: Hurricane Simon continues to intensify, Mexico catastrophe bond on watch - Artemis.bm Hurricane Simon continues to intensify, Mexico catastrophe bond on watch - Artemis.bm Hurricane Simon continues to intensify, Mexico catastrophe bond on watch 10th October 2026 - Author: Steve Evans Hurricane Simon in the Pacific is rapidly intensifying and seen as having a chance of sustaining major hurricane strength when it makes landfall on the Mexico coastline on Sunday, which has brought the $175 million IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric catastrophe bond back into focus again. Update – Oct 10th, 09:00 UTC: Hurricane Simon is a little stronger at 145 mph sustained winds, while the minimum central pressure is now estimated at 942mb. New forecast advisory data from the NHC shows hurricane Simon is still expected to become a very strong Category 4 or even a Category 5 hurricane later today. It seems from the data though, that less weakening is now anticipated prior to landfall, with the forecast advisory data suggesting Simon could reach landfall still at Category 4 wind speeds. Our sources suggest that hurricane Simon could now get closer to the low-levels of central pressure required to trigger Mexico’s parametric catastrophe bond. But, how much the storm can intensify today matters, as well as any weakening that occurs before it crosses into one of the parametric boxes. One projection we’ve seen calls for the central pressure of hurricane Simon to be in the 930mb’s when it crosses the cat bond’s parametric grid. As we said yesterday, we believe it may need to fall to 932mb or lower for a 25% payout to come due. At this stage we’re told it could just be a few millibars away. Mexico’s $175 million parametric IBRD Pacific named storm catastrophe bond is on watch again with this storm. We’ll update you later today. Update – Oct 10th, 07:00 UTC: Hurricane Simon has continued to intensify as forecast, with the latest NHC data showing a dangerous Category 4 storm with 140 mph winds, higher gusts and now a central pressure much lower at an estimated 945mb. The NHC says that, “Additional rapid strengthening is expected during the next day or so. Simon is forecast to approach the of west-central Mexico as a major hurricane this evening or Sunday.” However, Simon is relatively small which could hold back its intensification somewhat, currently hurricane force winds only extend outward around 15 miles from its centre. So it remains to be seen whether the central pressure can continue to deepen sufficiently to really threaten Mexico’s catastrophe bond. In addition, the forecast advisory data from 03:00 UTC today shows hurricane Simon reaching sustained winds of around 155 mph near its peak, but then weakening slightly prior to landfall with wind speeds of around 135-140 mph prior to landfall. So it could near or reach Category 5 status for a time, but weaken back to Category 4 or less at landfall. Remember though, the parametric zones for the Mexico Pacific named storm parametric cat bond are slightly offshore, not on the coastline, so it is the central pressure at the time any hurricane crosses one of the parametric zones that matters. At this stage hurricane Simon will need watching through Saturday, to see how intense it can become and whether it is likely to pose a threat to Mexico’s IBRD cat bond on nearing landfall. Update – 18:00 UTC: The NHC’s latest update and forecast advisory data shows hurricane Simon now with sustained winds of 100 mph and higher gusts. The all-important (for the cat bond) central pressure is now down to 973mb. The NHC said Simon should intensify rapidly now and approach Mexico’s coast as a dangerous major hurricane, strengthening through into Saturday. There are suggestions in the forecast data that hurricane Simon could have sustained winds of around 130 mph very close to making landfall. How long the intensification continues will have ramifications for how much the storm weakens. Although it’s important to remember that for Mexico’s cat bond to face a trigger event, it would need the minimum central pressure to deepen considerably, by perhaps 40mb or more. Only a couple of weeks ago in September this parametric catastrophe bond faced a threat from hurricane Polo, a storm that intensified rapidly and whose minimum central pressure deepened to levels required to activate the cat bond’s parametric trigger, but Polo weakened and in the end made landfall posing no threat of a loss . While many in the market are closely watching the Atlantic side with hurricane Isaias strengthening in the Gulf of Mexico , hurricane Simon in the Pacific is just the latest storm on that side to undergo rapid intensification and could even have the potential to pose the bigger cat bond market threat, albeit with only a single tranche of notes from the Mexico IBRD deal exposed to the storm. Hurricane Simon is currently a category 1 storm with sustained winds of 90 mph and a minimum central pressure of 978mb, as of the NHC’s 12:00 UTC update today. However, that update explains that Simon is rapidly intensifying and expected to become a major hurricane today. The NHC said, “Rapid intensification is expected to continue, and Simon is expected to be a very dangerous major hurricane when it approaches the coast of Mexico. “Simon’s small, intense inner core, favorable environmental conditions, low shear, very warm oceanic temperatures, and high mid-level moisture content all support a rapid intensification event, which appears to be well underway. Further significant strengthening is expected, and the cyclone is forecast to be a very dangerous major hurricane when it approaches the coast of Mexico. The guidance also shows compact Simon quickly weakening and over the high mountainous terrain by early next week. The NHC forecast is once again hedged toward the high end of the guidance, in best agreement with the HFIP-HCCA model.” The NHC’s forecast advisory data as of the same time shows hurricane Simon attaining sustained wind speeds of up to 145 mph as it approaches the Mexico coastline, albeit with some weakening expected as it closes in on landfall, which is expected to be in the southwestern and west-central region of Mexico on Sunday. The forecast cone shows hurricane Simon making landfall as a Category 3 major storm, but with rapid intensification underway it remains to be seen how strong this storm can become, given the very conducive conditions it is passing through of very warm waters and low shear. Currently, many forecast models do not seem to have re-calibrated to take account of the rapid intensification currently underway with hurricane Simon. Once they do, we should have a clearer picture of how low the central pressure could drop as it moves towards Mexico and landfall. You can see hurricane Simon’s current position and the forecast in the graphic below from Tomer Burg’s PolarWx: At a minimum central pressure of 978mb at this time, hurricane Simon is still well-above the levels required to trigger Mexico’s parametric IBRD Pacific named storm catastrophe bond. But the forecast takes it directly ashore at landfall, so it will likely pass through the parametric trigger zones that run along Mexico’s coastline, just offshore. The $175 million of IBRD CAR Mexico 2024 (Pacific) parametric catastrophe bond notes feature a parametric trigger design that requires a storm to have a minimum central pressure at or below specific levels in order to trigger a payout if it moves across the parametric grid lines. Different areas of coastline have different payout factors attached to them as well, so location and intensity are the two key metrics for defining whether any payout will occur and those payouts can be from 25% of principal, right up to the full 100% or $175 million, depending on where any hurricane breaches the parametric box and how intense it is (how low the pressure falls). For the cat bond to be triggered at all, the initial central pressure threshold is at 937mb or lower for the parametric zones, albeit that the exact location matters for what kind of payout that could result in. Sources we’ve spoken with suggest, based on the forecast landfall region for hurricane Simon, a central pressure of 932mb or lower may be required to trigger a 25% payout for the cat bond, while a much lower pressure would be required for any payout to be at 50% to 100% of the cat bond principal. Sources also suggest that, based on the current NHC data, Simon may deepen to 940mb prior to landfall, although that obviously comes with uncertainty and pressures can be lower than expected, while how much rapid intensification is actually seen will clearly be a factor over the coming hours. It remains uncertain at this time whether hurricane Simon will intensify sufficiently to see its minimum central pressure decline to the levels required to trigger Mexico’s parametric cat bond. It seems that in order for a triggering event to occur, hurricane Simon would need to intensify further than the latest NHC forecast data suggests, this will require watching for. But, given the NHC forecast and the rapid intensification deemed underway, it clearly has the potential to pose a threat, meaning catastrophe bond market participants are likely now watching both Pacific (Simon) and Atlantic sides ( Isaias ). items.extracted_text: Hurricane Isaias forecast to hit Cat 3 then weaken, single-digit billion insured losses still likely - Artemis.bm Hurricane Isaias forecast to hit Cat 3 then weaken, single-digit billion insured losses still likely - Artemis.bm Hurricane Isaias forecast to hit Cat 3 then weaken, single-digit billion insured losses still likely 9th October 2026 - Author: Steve Evans Hurricane Isaias is now forecast to intensify further to become a major Category 3 storm as it approaches the Gulf Coast today, outpacing meteorologists initial expectations. But, prior to landfall late today or early on Saturday, Isaias is expected to encounter wind shear and begin to weaken, which should lessen the impacts and keeps estimates in the single-digit billions. Final update – Oct 10th, 07:00 UTC: Hurricane Isaias made landfall close to Destin, Florida at 01:30 UTC (8.30pm CDT) on Saturday morning as a Category 2 storm, with sustained winds of 105 mph and higher gusts. Wind gusts of 116 mph were reported at onshore WeatherFlow stations, with 100 mph plus gusts recorded elsewhere along the immediate landfall area of Gulf coastline and more widely 80 mph gusts recorded. In addition, water levels of between 5 to 6 feet above normal were recorded by gauges in Panama City Beach, Florida. Isaias is now moving inland and transitioning to extra-tropical, sustained winds are now closer to 60 mph, but it is now bringing flash-flooding risk from rainfall and a threat of tornadoes and severe weather to a wide area as it moves north. In the end, Isaias panned out to be slightly stronger than had initially been forecast on landfall, but still industry expectations of a low to mid-single-digit billion dollar insurance industry loss event appear likely to prove accurate. Update – 17:15 UTC: Gallagher Re has updated its analysis to say that, “Based on an assessment of exposure extending from Mobile (Alabama) to Destin (Florida), anticipated coastal and inland wind speeds, and historical landfalls from high-end Category 2 or low-end Category 3 hurricanes in this region, it is anticipated that insured losses, including private insurance carrier and National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) claims payouts, would be expected to settle in the mid-single-digit billions (USD). Given abundant reinsurance market capital, this event is unlikely to meaningfully influence upcoming January 1 reinsurance renewal discussions.” It’s worth noting there that the “low” to mid-single digit is now just mid-single digits, suggesting a slightly higher loss forecast from the reinsurance broker. Update – 16:00 UTC: Andrew Siffert of BMS Group has written in his latest update, “As stated yesterday, the landfall location, intensity, and overall structure of Isaias remain uncertain even with landfall about 12 hours away. Still, based on what we know, historical analogs like Hurricane Sally (2020), and catastrophe model runs, the losses today should be higher. This is simply because the expected landfall location is farther east, with a stronger storm near Pensacola, FL. Losses should be below $10B, with an expected range of $4B to $6B today. However, as shown in the loss difference between Sally (2020) and Ivan (2004), there can be exponentially higher losses with a stronger storm, which is why how strong Isaias gets today and how fast it moves forward, will determine how much time it has to weaken before landfall due to drier air and wind shear. In leading catastrophe risk model event sets, 80% of Category 1 events impacting the Pensacola, FL region result in industry losses below $3B, but when adjusted to Category 2 events, losses jump to $17B. So, losses are quite sensitive to overall landfall intensity, and while insurance industry losses for Isaias increased, this still does not seem to materially affect current capacity or the softer market conditions in the U.S. property insurance market.” In addition, reinsurance broker Marsh Re has said, “Based on historical events, Isaias has the potential to generate insured losses in the mid single digits of billions of USD. Opal, Dennis and Eloise are the best matches.” Update – 15:00 UTC: No change to hurricane Isaias’ intensity and pressure in the 15:00 UTC update from the NHC, being still 120 mph sustained winds and 959mb. But, the NHC now states that Isaias could be stronger on landfall than was assumed earlier today. They explain, “Fluctuations in intensity are possible through this afternoon, but Isaias is expected to be at or near major hurricane strength when it makes landfall this evening. Weakening is expected beginning tonight after Isaias makes landfall, and the storm is likely to become post-tropical by late Saturday.” That clearly has ramifications for the potential insurance market loss and the stronger the storm at landfall, the more chance there is of reinsurance and potentially ILS structures supporting the recovery from the storm financially. So, hurricane Isaias could potentially be a strong Cat 2 or even weak Cat 3 landfall event and as Twelve Securis highlighted (see below) that could take industry losses towards higher single digit billions or above, depending on the exact landfall location and damage that occurs. Notably, for those in the path of Isaias, a stronger storm will be more of a threat to lives and property, both from winds and potentially also surge too. The NHC warns of life-threatening storm surge and damaging winds across the landfall region. Update – 14:45 UTC: Cat bond and ILS investment manager Twelve Securis has commented on hurricane Isaias, “Historical events with comparable tracks and intensity profiles include Hurricanes Sally (2020), Erin (1995) and Opal (1995). Category 1 hurricanes making landfall in this region have historically generated industry losses ranging from hundreds of millions to low-single digit billions of US dollars, while Category 2 events have resulted in losses in the low- to mid-single digit billions. “Based on current forecasts, an outcome comparable to Hurricane Sally, with insured losses in the mid-single digit billions of US dollars, is considered the most likely scenario. However, considerable uncertainty remains regarding the precise landfall location and intensity. Should Isaias strengthen more than anticipated, a scenario closer to Hurricane Opal, with insured losses exceeding USD 10bn, cannot be ruled out, although this is currently considered less likely.” Update – 13:00 UTC: The NHC has just declared hurricane Isaias a major Category 3 storm, with sustained winds of 120 mph and higher gusts. The storms minimum central pressure has been measured at 959mb by a dropsonde. Update – 12:00 UTC: Hurricane Isaias continues to have maximum sustained winds of 110 mph, but its central pressure has deepened a little to 958mb, according to the NHC. The Center continues to forecast Isaias will become a major hurricane soon and be a dangerous although weakening storm at landfall. The NHC has now raised its storm surge forecast values slightly, with between 6 and 9 feet now expected from the Alabama/Florida border to Grayton Beach, FL, and surge heights of 4 to 7 feet more widely between Dauphin Island, AL and Steinhatchee River, FL. Update – 09:00 UTC: A new update from the NHC shows hurricane Isaias is a little stronger with sustained winds of 110 mph (top-end Category 2) and a central pressure currently estimated at 963mb. The storm is intensifying and the NHC reiterated, “Isaias is likely to become a major hurricane this morning. Slight weakening is expected before landfall, but it is expected to remain a dangerous hurricane.” New forecast advisory date from the NHC now shows hurricane Isaias reaching sustained winds of around 120 mph (major Category 3 strength) with gusts as high as 150 mph as it moves north through the Gulf, but still weakening as it nears landfall. Moody’s has said this morning that its data shows 31,659 commercial properties in Alabama, Florida and Mississippi have a greater than 50% probability of facing winds of at least 50 mph from hurricane Isaias, which is the threshold at which some damage is likely. These properties have a total estimated value of $71.8 billion. There are 14,945 multi-family residential buildings with an estimated value of $40.2 billion within that data, while retail, office and industrial are the other commercial property types most exposed. Moody’s also said that the top cities expected to be impacted by Hurricane Isaias include: Mobile, AL Pensacola, FL and Biloxi, MS. James Cosgrove, Associate Director-Moody’s RMS Event Response, Moody’s commented, “Isaias is the first hurricane of the 2026 North Atlantic hurricane season and represents the latest point in the calendar year that the first hurricane has formed. The last hurricane to make landfall in the coastal region that spans Mississippi, Alabama, and the western Florida Panhandle was Hurricane Sally in September 2020, which made landfall as a Category 2 hurricane near Gulf Shores, Alabama, just west of Pensacola, Florida. Sally’s landfall parameters and landfall location are not too dissimilar to the current forecast for Isaias. “Note that Sally itself was the first hurricane to make landfall in Alabama since Ivan in 2004 (though Alabama has a narrow coastline for such occurrences to be recorded). Also prior to Sally, Hurricane Nate made landfall as a weak Category 1 hurricane near the mouth of the Mississippi River in Biloxi, Mississippi in October 2017. Nate was weaker and further west than the forecast for Isaias.” Hurricane Isaias has outpaced meteorologist expectations for a number of reasons. At first, when the depression was forming, many had said they did not anticipate the storm to form as quickly as it did. Now, having spent days forecasting a low-end Category 2 hurricane at Isaia’s peak, the forecasts have changed as Isaias has intensified a little more than anticipated. Currently, as of the 06:00 UTC update from the National Hurricane Center, Isaias has maximum sustained winds of 105 mph, which puts it as a Category 2 storm at this time. Hurricane Isaias has stronger gusts and a minimum central pressure that is estimated at 972mb, while the storm is currently around 230 miles south of the mouth of the Mississippi River. Isaias is now forecast to move north-northeast and then turn to the north, before making landfall on the northern Gulf Coast late tonight, or early Saturday morning. The NHC said, “Isaias could briefly become a major hurricane later today. Although some weakening is forecast thereafter, Isaias will remain a dangerous hurricane as it approaches the northern Gulf Coast tonight.” The chart below from Tomer Burg’s PolarWx service shows the current NHC forecast including cone and wind speeds (this should update to show the latest hurricane information): The latest forecast advisory data is still from 03:00 UTC, but that predicts hurricane Isaias will reach sustained winds of 100 knots, which would put it as a Category 3 major hurricane as it approaches landfall. But, the forecast weakening is evident in the data as well, with sustained winds of just under 100 mph and gusts of around 120 mph expected just prior to landfall, hence this would be a low-end Category 2 landfall event if that turns out to be accurate. Of course, hurricane Isaias has tended to outperform, so there is still some uncertainty. But wind shear is in its path and it is difficult to see it maintaining structure and so strength as it nears landfall, weakening does look backed in at this time. The forecast storm surge remains for around 6 to 7 foot maximums, with the coastline between Dauphin Island, Alabama to Indian Pass, Florida expected to see the peak. Localised rainfall totals of up to 15 inches, more widely 4 to 8 inches are also warned, while the threat of tornadoes as hurricane Isaias moves ashore and inland is also considered a risk. items.extracted_text: Texas Reports Homeowners and Auto Rate Decreases Article 1 Comment Homeowners insurance rates are beginning to come down in Texas, according to the most recent data from the state insurance department. Since the start of July, insurance companies have filed an average 4.3% rate decrease on homeowners policies. ASI Lloyds, a Progressive company, filed a 6% rate decrease impacting 71,000 policyholders, and Texas Farm Bureau Mutual Insurance Company filed a 5.2% rate decrease, impacting 133,000 policyholders. Insurance Commissioner Amanda Crawford said the department is “pleased to see some relief beginning to reach the market.” “As rates moderate, Texans should take advantage of the competitive market, shop around, and make sure they’re getting the best value for their coverage,” Crawford said. Some Texas drivers are also seeing decreases on their auto insurance rates. Auto Club County Mutual Insurance Company filed a 3% rate decrease, impacting 235,000 policyholders, and Loya Insurance Company filed a 10.3% rate decrease, impacting 39,000 policyholders, the insurance department said. items.extracted_text: Hurricane Isaias Reaches Cat 3 Status as Insurers, Adjusters, Property Owners Prepare Article 0 Comments Isaias suddenly strengthened into a Category 3 hurricane as of Friday morning, Oct. 9, and remained on course to hit the Pensacola-Panhandle area of Florida with more than six feet of storm surge, strong winds and as much as 15 inches of rainfall. “Just-received data from an Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicate that Isaias has strengthened to a major hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 120 mph (195 km/h) with higher gusts,” the National Hurricane Center said in update early Oct. 9. Click to enlarge map. The storm, the first hurricane of the unusually quiet 2026 Atlantic hurricane season, was expected to weaken quickly as it comes ashore. It could be downgraded to a tropical stormy by the afternoon of Oct. 10 as it moves due north into Alabama, the NHC noted . But initially, Friday night could bring significant wind and flood damage to parts of the coast. “Preparations should be rushed to completion as the weather will go downhill quickly today,” the Hurricane Center said. “While the storm is not expected to make landfall at peak intensity, it is likely that Isaias will still be a significant hurricane when it reaches the coast.” NHC meteorologist Robbie Berg called it a “life-threatening situation,” Bloomberg reported . “Persons located within these areas should take all necessary actions to protect life and property from rising water and the potential for other dangerous conditions.” Rain and gusting winds already were being felt early Friday morning in the Pensacola area, as homeowners and businesses worked to board up windows and fill sandbags. The strengthening of the storm is expected to trigger insurance claims-handling firms and property insurers to prepare to deploy adjusters and claims teams to the Florida Panhandle, adjusters said. Click to enlarge. Source: NFIP “Mangrove Property Insurance Company has activated its catastrophe plan as Hurricane Isaias approaches,” an official with the Tampa-based insurer said in an email. “Once conditions are safe, policyholders should document damage with photographs or video, retain receipts for emergency repairs and related expenses, take reasonable steps to prevent further damage without putting themselves at risk.” Mangrove holds about 3,900 policies in a 10-county area expected to be most affected by the storm winds, more than $1.5 billion in exposure, Florida Office of Insurance Regulation data show. The storm system is forecast to bring flash flooding and spawn tornadoes, the Hurricane Center said. If flooding is extensive, relatively few property owners outside the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s Special Flood Hazard Area are covered by flood insurance. National Flood Insurance Program data show that in Escambia County, the most populated county in the Panhandle, about 8% of residential property was covered by the program, as of August. In the Special Flood Hazard Area in the county, the low-lying areas most likely to flood, however, 62% of residential structures carried the flood insurance. “The shallow, gently sloping seafloor along the projected landfall area makes the region especially vulnerable to significant storm surge,” said Jeff Waters, director of North Atlantic hurricane models for Moody’s, the financial rating and analytics firm. “ Isaias is forecast to strengthen quickly and push damaging winds well-inland before weakening. That puts communities beyond the immediate Gulf coast at risk.” Moody’s also reported that 31,659 commercial properties, with a total estimated value of $72 billion, have a high probability of seeing winds of at least 50mph during the storm. Of those properties, almost 15,000 are multi-family residential buildings valued at $40 billion. items.extracted_text: Hurricane Isaias Reaches Category 3 as It Nears Florida, Alabama Article 0 Comments Hurricane Isaias strengthened into a major storm Friday as it barreled toward more than 3 million people along the U.S. Gulf Coast, threatening dangerous flooding and storm surge after forcing energy producers to curb output. Isaias’ top winds reached 120 miles (193 kilometers) per hour, making it a Category 3 storm on the five-step Saffir-Simpson scale, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said in a special update at 8:20 a.m. New York time. The storm was about 240 miles south of Pensacola, Florida. The hurricane is expected to make landfall late Friday or early Saturday along the Alabama-Florida coast. Storm surge and tropical storm warnings extend west into Louisiana. In addition to its damaging winds, Isaias is forecast to push as much as 9 feet (3 meters) of water ashore, the center said. Plywood is placed over the windows of a restaurant in Gulf Breeze, Florida on Oct. 8. Photographer: Joe Raedle/Getty Images “This is a life threatening situation,” Robbie Berg, a warning coordination meteorologist at the center, wrote in his outlook. “Persons located within these areas should take all necessary actions to protect life and property from rising water and the potential for other dangerous conditions.” Isaias helped push U.S. oil prices up as much as 5.6% on Thursday as companies evacuated crews from platforms and moved drilling rigs out of the storm’s path. Roughly 63% of U.S. Gulf of Mexico crude output has been shut in, while nearly 500,000 barrels a day of refining capacity lies in or near the storm’s projected path. Several ports are also shutting ahead of the hurricane, disrupting seaborne crude deliveries. Three fuel-making facilities are in or near the projected path, including Chevron Corp.’s 356,000 barrel-a-day refinery in Pascagoula, Mississippi. Even small production losses could trigger sharp price increases, with U.S. gasoline and diesel stockpiles already far below seasonal norms. Natural gas production in the Gulf has also fallen, with about 57% of regional output shut in. Still, Isaias’s shift east has limited the hit to Gulf oil, gas and LNG facilities compared with earlier forecasts, even as the storm intensified, according to Gary Cunningham at Tradition Energy. “Isaias is remaining stronger than originally projected but its track is more east,” Cunningham said in an email, limiting the impact on Gulf production and LNG export facilities. Natural gas futures fell Friday as traders weighed the production losses against the potential for storm damage to curb regional energy demand. November gas was trading near $3.14 per million British thermal units Friday morning, after settling at $3.168 Thursday. Florida suspended tolls on bridges in Okaloosa and Santa Rosa counties to help people evacuate, while Governor Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency in 27 counties. After coming ashore, Isaias is forecast to race across Alabama and into the Tennessee and Ohio valleys, bringing as much as 8 to 12 inches of rain, said Tyler Roys, a meteorologist with commercial forecaster AccuWeather Inc. On the storm’s eastern side, as much as 8 inches may fall across parts of the Carolinas, including areas devastated by flooding from Hurricane Helene in 2024. Duke Energy’s Florida utility said workers are ready to respond to outages. “Our crews are prepared to restore power as soon as conditions allow,” said Todd Fountain, the utility’s storm director. At the same time, Tropical Storm Rachel is forecast to strike northern Baja California late Saturday, sending heavy rain and damaging wind gusts into Southern California, Arizona and as far north as Salt Lake City, Utah, Roys said. A shift in the track could bring the storm closer to San Diego, which would be a rare event. “We cannot rule out isolated tornadoes in southeast Arizona,” Roys said. items.title: Pumpkin disclaimer: personality not included
items.original_title: Pumpkin disclaimer: personality not included
items.rss_title: Pumpkin disclaimer: personality not included
items.rss_description: The scariest thing in the Halloween candy aisle may be that we actually need the fine print regarding faceless Reese’s Peanut Butter Pumpkins.
items.extracted_text: A seasonal favorite is getting a packaging update after a lawsuit over missing faces. The chocolate still has no eyes or mouth. The wrapper, however, has learned to speak lawyer. “Carving not on actual product,” it now warns beside the grinning pumpkin pictured on the signature orange package, Fox Business reported. The change follows Hershey’s successful defense against a proposed class action brought by two Florida consumers who said they bought the candy for its decorative designs and received something less expressive. Nathan Vidal and Eduardo Granados alleged they overpaid for the faceless treats, arguing that the pictured pumpkins’ appeal justified their purchases. Apparently, a peanut butter filling cannot fill every emotional void. A federal judge in Miami dismissed the case, finding the plaintiffs lacked standing to claim they overpaid. Their alleged injury amounted to “subjective disappointment,” she wrote, also noting that the missing carvings did not make the candy defective, worthless, or devoid of economic value. In other words, still edible. Just terrible at making eye contact. items.title: Falcons exempt from California comp claim over player’s cumulative injuries
items.original_title: Falcons exempt from California comp claim over player’s cumulative injuries
items.rss_title: Falcons exempt from California comp claim over player’s cumulative injuries
items.rss_description: A California appeals court on Wednesday ruled that a professional football team was exempt from liability under the state’s workers compensation law for a former player’s cumulative injury claim, despite his earlier employment with a California team.
items.extracted_text: Wayne Gandy, who played 15 NFL seasons before retiring in February 2009, filed a California workers compensation claim in September 2015 alleging cumulative injuries to multiple body parts. He named several former teams, including the Atlanta Falcons, in the claim addressed in Atlanta Falcons v. Workers’ Compensation Appeals Board , decided by the California Court of Appeal, Fourth Appellate District, Division Three. Mr. Gandy signed a contract in California with the Los Angeles Rams in 1994 and continued under that contract after the team moved to St. Louis. He later played for Pittsburgh, New Orleans and Atlanta. The compensation appeals board concluded that his California hiring gave it jurisdiction regardless of statutory exemptions for professional athletes. The appeals court rejected that interpretation. The Falcons provided workers compensation coverage under another state’s laws that also covered Mr. Gandy’s work in California. He performed fewer than 20% of his duty days in California during the relevant period, satisfying an exemption for athletes temporarily working in the state. The court also found that his career did not satisfy the conditions for avoiding a separate exemption: He played only one season for a California-based team, spent fewer than 20% of his career duty days in California or with a California-based team, and played at least seven seasons for non-California teams. The court annulled the board’s decision and remanded the matter. Its ruling addressed only the Falcons’ liability, not that of Mr. Gandy’s other former teams. items.extracted_text: Avec 11,5 milliards d’euros de cotisations en août 2026, l’assurance vie demeure un levier essentiel pour financer l’économie française et européenne - France Assureurs À 11,5 milliards d’euros, les cotisations en assurance vie sont en baisse de −6 % en août 2026 par rapport au même mois de 2025. Les prestations du mois d’août 2026 s’élèvent à 9,5 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +15 % par rapport à août 2025. Elles atteignent ainsi leur plus haut niveau depuis trois ans pour un mois d’août. La collecte nette s’établit à +2,0 milliards d’euros, en baisse de −1,9 milliard d’euros par rapport à celle d’août 2025. Depuis le début de l’année, elle s’élève à +43,5 milliards d’euros, supérieure de +6,9 milliards d’euros à celle de 2025 sur la même période. En août 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 11,5 milliards d’euros, en diminution de −6 % par rapport au même mois de 2025 où les cotisations avaient atteint un niveau exceptionnellement élevé (12,2 milliards d’euros, soit +27 % par rapport à août 2024). Les cotisations progressent de +3 % pour les supports en unités de compte (UC) mais diminuent pour les supports en euros (−10 %). Depuis début 2026, les cotisations atteignent 138,7 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +9,2 milliards d’euros, soit +7 % par rapport aux huit premiers mois de 2025. Cette dynamique positive concerne principalement les supports en UC (+10 %) et dans une moindre mesure ceux en euros (+5 %). La part des UC dans les cotisations s’établit à 37 % sur le mois d’août 2026 et se maintient à 40 % sur les huit premiers mois de l’année. À 9,5 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois d’août 2026 sont en hausse de +15 % par rapport à août 2025. Cette augmentation est portée essentiellement par les supports en UC (+27 %), tandis que ceux en euros enregistrent une hausse de +11 %. Les prestations atteignent ainsi leur plus haut niveau pour un mois d’août depuis trois ans, avec notamment 2,4 milliards d’euros de prestations sur les supports en UC. Depuis le début de l’année, les prestations s’élèvent à 95,2 milliards d’euros, en légère progression de +2,3 milliards d’euros, soit +2 % par rapport aux huit premiers mois de 2025. Cette dynamique concerne principalement les supports en UC qui augmentent de +1,5 milliard d’euros, tandis que les prestations des supports en euros sont en hausse de +0,8 milliard d’euros. La collecte nette s’établit donc à +2,0 milliards d’euros en août 2026. Les supports en UC représentent l’essentiel de cette dynamique, avec une collecte nette positive de +1,9 milliard d’euros, tandis que les supports en euros enregistrent une collecte positive de +0,2 milliard d’euros. Depuis le début de l’année, la collecte nette s’élève à +43,5 milliards d’euros, supérieure de +6,9 milliards d’euros à celle de 2025 sur la même période. Les supports en UC concentrent une partie très majoritaire de cette collecte nette (+33,9 milliards d’euros), tandis que ceux en euros y contribuent à hauteur de +9,7 milliards d’euros. L’encours des contrats d’assurance vie atteint 2 171 milliards d’euros à fin août 2026, en hausse de +5,7 % sur un an (+117 milliards d’euros). Selon Paul ESMEIN, directeur général de France Assureurs : «En août 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie demeurent à un niveau élevé, à 11,5 milliards d’euros. Depuis le début de l’année, la dynamique de l’assurance vie confirme la confiance des Français dans ce produit d’épargne de long terme, qui leur permet de préparer leur avenir, tout en contribuant au financement de l’économie française. Avec 80 % de ses encours investis au sein de l’Union européenne et plus de la moitié sur le territoire français, l’assurance vie constitue un levier essentiel au service de la souveraineté nationale et européenne. » Pour en savoir plus sur l’assurance vie, cliquez ici. NB : l’arrondi d’un total ou d’une différence n’est pas nécessairement égal à la somme ou à la différence des arrondis de ses composantes. C’est parfois le cas entre la collecte nette d’une part et la différence entre les cotisations et les prestations d’autre part, lorsque ces grandeurs sont toutes trois arrondies en milliards d’euros. items.extracted_text: San Antonio Car Dealerships to Pay $430K In Sex Discrimination Lawsuit Article 0 Comments Benson Enterprises, Inc., the operator of automotive dealerships including Ingram Park Chrysler Jeep Dodge Ram in San Antonio, will pay $430,000 and furnish other relief to settle a sex-based harassment and retaliation lawsuit filed by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), the federal agency announced. According to the EEOC’s lawsuit, from January to June 2021, a male manager for Ingram Park Chrysler Jeep Dodge Ram created and maintained a hostile work environment by subjecting a female fleet service advisor to frequent and offensive sexist comments about her and other women, such as statements that women were ignorant, lazy or unqualified to work as service advisors. The suit charged that the manager also directed clients away from the fleet service advisor and excluded her from important communications regarding business operations — resulting in a loss of sales and negatively affecting her commission-based compensation. Additionally, the manager excluded the fleet service advisor and another female employee from an employee group chat announcing competitions for monetary bonuses, resulting in denial of earnings opportunities based on sex. The lawsuit also charged that the fleet services advisor made several reports to the dealership about the male manager’s discriminatory conduct, and the dealership subsequently fired her on June 11, 2021 in retaliation for those complaints and because of her sex. This alleged conduct violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which prohibits sex-based workplace harassment and discrimination in the terms and conditions of employment and further prohibits retaliation against employees who report or oppose such practices. The EEOC filed suit (U.S. EEOC v. Benson Enterprises, Inc., et al., Case No. 5:24-cv-01072) in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, San Antonio Division after first attempting to reach a pre-litigation settlement through its administrative conciliation process. items.extracted_text: LCB-FT : un guide pour connaître les informations, justificatifs et données personnelles que votre professionnel de l’assurance peut vous demander - France Assureurs Les professionnels du secteur financier (banques, assurances…) participent à la lutte contre le blanchiment d’argent et le financement du terrorisme (LCB-FT), notamment parce qu’ils gèrent des produits d’épargne sur lesquels pourraient être versés des fonds issus ou destinés à ces activités illégales. La réglementation relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux et le financement du terrorisme (LCB-FT) leur impose de mettre en œuvre des mesures de vigilance. Ils doivent notamment vérifier l’identité de leurs clients, connaître leur situation et exercer un contrôle sur leurs opérations afin d’identifier celles qui pourraient présenter un risque. Concrètement, votre assureur peut être amené à vous demander des informations sur votre situation personnelle et professionnelle, votre patrimoine ou encore vos revenus. Il peut également vous interroger sur l’origine des fonds versés sur un contrat d’assurance vie, ainsi que sur la destination ou l’utilisation des sommes versées lors du dénouement de ce contrat par exemple. Ce guide, réalisé par AGEA, France Assureurs et Planète CSCA, a pour objectif d’expliquer aux assurés les raisons pour lesquelles les professionnels de l’assurance leur demandent des informations, justificatifs et données personnelles. items.extracted_text: Nouvel épisode d’Assurément Margaux – Assurance scolaire : obligatoire… ou pas ? - France Assureurs Alors que son week-end à Noirmoutier prend un tournant inattendu, Margaux fait la connaissance de Carole, la sœur de Simon. De quoi rassurer les parents… bien au-delà de la cour de récréation. L’assurance scolaire est-elle obligatoire ? Que couvre-t-elle en cas d’accident ? Comment choisir une couverture adaptée aux activités de son enfant ? Un épisode qui répond aux questions que beaucoup de parents se posent… souvent le jour où un imprévu survient. items.extracted_text: Nouvel épisode d’Assurément Margaux – Vacances : et si rien ne se passait comme prévu ? - France Assureurs Un week-end en solo à Noirmoutier après une rupture, une panne de voiture dès l’arrivée… et des vacances qui commencent décidément très mal. Heureusement, chaque galère est aussi l’occasion pour Margaux de découvrir qu’il existe des solutions pour faire face aux imprévus. Au fil de son séjour, elle réalise que plusieurs assurances peuvent intervenir selon les situations : une panne de voiture, un voyage annulé, une hospitalisation ou encore un sinistre à son domicile pendant les vacances. Un épisode pour comprendre quelles garanties peuvent réellement vous accompagner avant, pendant… et parfois même après votre départ. Que faire en cas de panne de voiture pendant ses vacances ? Dans quels cas une assurance annulation peut-elle intervenir ? Quelles assurances et services d’assistance peuvent vous aider face aux imprévus d’un voyage ? Un épisode qui rappelle qu’on prépare souvent ses vacances dans les moindres détails… mais qu’un rapide coup d’œil à ses contrats peut aussi faire toute la différence. Transcription de l’épisode Vous savez pas ce qui m’est arrivé la semaine dernière ? Je devais partir en weekend en amoureux… et à la place mon couple a été mis en pause. Génial non ? Ah on aime ça. Ben je vais vous dire, j’suis montée dans la voiture et j’suis partie quand même. Noirmoutier, me voilà ! Ok, donc je roule, je pleure, je chante du Céline Dion et je repleure, et je roule. Mais quand j’arrive sur l’île, là, il se passe un truc bizarre. Bruit chelou, voyant rouge… bam, la panne. Je me retrouve sur le bord de la route, avec ma valise et une mouette qui me regarde galérer. Salut copine. Bon, j’appelle le numéro d’urgence — heu oui, la voiture est assurée, on avait checké avant de partir avec Chloé — et j’avais même pris l’option en cas de panne en bas de chez moi. Et hop, en quelques minutes, le remorquage est organisé. D’ailleurs, j’sais pas si vous savez, mais selon le contrat, si la panne avait été plus grave, grâce à l’assistance j’aurais pu être hébergée sur place, bénéficier d’un rapatriement… ou même avoir un chauffeur pour ramener la voiture. C’est bon ça, non ? Là, on parle de l’assistance liée à la voiture, mais selon les contrats que tu as, il peut aussi y’avoir d’autres formes d’assistance auxquelles on pense pas toujours – par exemple, dans certains contrats habitation, si un gros sinistre arrive chez toi pendant que t’es en vacances, l’assistance peut organiser une aide à domicile – comme quelques heures de ménage ou une aide ponctuelle pour gérer le quotidien. Bref, tout dépend des contrats que t’as souscrits… et c’est pour ça que ça vaut le coup de vérifier avant de partir. Donc moi je suis là, j’attends le dépanneur. Il commence mal mon weekend solo. J’hésite à tout laisser tomber… Et d’un coup ça me fait penser à l’assurance annulation. Quand on réserve un voyage, ben ça marche seulement dans des cas bien précis : maladie, accident, sinistre grave à la maison ou certains gros problèmes de transport prévus au contrat. En revanche pour mon chagrin d’amour… ben non évidemment ! Bon, allez, quoi qu’il en soit cette assurance annulation, elle peut déjà être incluse dans le prix du voyage, parfois proposée par l’agence en option… et parfois liée à ta carte bancaire. Oui, oui ! Mais vérifie bien les conditions et garanties ! Certains – comme moi – préfèrent carrément une assurance voyage spécifique, qui peut couvrir aussi la responsabilité civile, les bagages… et inclure des services d’assistance – par exemple en cas d’hospitalisation longue, avec l’organisation de la venue d’un proche — transport, hébergement… oui, oui ! Et vous savez pourquoi je préfère ? Parce que je suis tête en l’air ! Vous croyez que c’est pour ça qu’il veut faire un break Mehdi ? Non attends, c’est pas un motif… surtout que en fait j’suis super prévoyante. En tout cas c’est fou le nombre de situations prévues ! Après, j’ai pas de mérite – c’est simple de se mettre à l’abri : il suffit de vérifier avant de partir ce qu’on a vraiment dans ses contrats : Qui est couvert ? Quelles exclusions ? Et est-ce qu’on a bien les bons numéros en cas d’urgence ? Bref, moi en tous cas, j’avais tout prévu… sauf que Mehdi me plante. Mais tu sais quoi ? Je vais me le faire, mon weekend. Tant pis pour lui. On est pas bien là ? Un bord de route, des mouettes, la mer… (Bruit de freins de voiture) (voix de Simon) « Ça va Margaux ? » Je me retourne, c’était Simon. Mon ex. À Noirmoutier. Au milieu de nulle part. (voix de Simon) « Attends, bouge pas, j’arrive… » « Heu oui je… heu… bah j’attends le dépanneur en fait. » (voix de Simon) « Et ben je vais te tenir compagnie. » Pour plus d’informations, rendez-vous sur le site de France Assureurs ! items.extracted_text: Avec 18,8 milliards d’euros de cotisations en juillet 2026, l’assurance vie maintient son cap au service du financement de l’économie - France Assureurs En juillet 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 18,8 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +1 % par rapport au même mois de 2025. À 14,1 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois de juillet 2026 sont en hausse de +4 % par rapport à juillet 2025. La collecte nette s’établit à +4,7 milliards d’euros, en baisse de −0,4 milliard d’euros par rapport à celle de juillet 2025. En juillet 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 18,8 milliards d’euros, en légère augmentation de +1 % par rapport au même mois de 2025. Elles dépassent ainsi le précédent record établi sur la même période l’an dernier (18,7 milliards d’euros). Les cotisations progressent pour les supports en unités de compte (UC, +5 %), cette dynamique étant en partie compensée par une baisse sur les supports en euros (−2%). Depuis début 2026, les cotisations atteignent 127,8 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +10,4 milliards d’euros, soit +9 % par rapport aux sept premiers mois de 2025. Cette dynamique positive concerne principalement les supports en UC (+11 %) et dans une moindre mesure ceux en euros (+8 %). La part des UC dans les cotisations s’établit à 42 % sur le mois de juillet 2026 et à 40 % sur les sept premiers mois de l’année. À 14,1 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois de juillet 2026 sont en hausse de +4 % par rapport à juillet 2025. Cette augmentation est portée essentiellement par les supports en UC (+8 %), tandis que ceux en euros enregistrent une hausse plus modérée (+2 %). Depuis le début de l’année, les prestations s’élèvent à 86,5 milliards d’euros, en légère progression de +1,8 milliard d’euros, soit +2 % par rapport aux sept premiers mois de 2025. Cette dynamique concerne principalement les supports en UC (+1,6 milliard d’euros), tandis que les prestations des supports en euros restent quasiment stables (+0,2 milliard d’euros). La collecte nette s’établit donc à +4,7 milliards d’euros, en baisse de −0,4 milliard d’euros par rapport à celle du même mois de l’année précédente. Les supports en euros enregistrent une collecte positive de +0,9 milliard d’euros et les supports en UC poursuivent également leur dynamique haussière (+3,8 milliards d’euros). Depuis le début de l’année, la collecte nette s’élève à +41,3 milliards d’euros, supérieure de +8,7 milliards d’euros à celle de 2025 sur la même période. Les supports en UC concentrent l’essentiel de cette collecte nette (+31,3 milliards d’euros), tandis ceux en euros y contribuent dans une moindre mesure (+10,0 milliards d’euros). L’encours des contrats d’assurance vie atteint 2 174 milliards d’euros à fin juillet 2026, en hausse de +6,3 % sur un an (+128 milliards d’euros). Selon Paul ESMEIN, directeur général de France Assureurs : « Avec un record de 18,8 milliards d’euros de cotisations en juillet, l’assurance vie confirme une nouvelle fois sa solidité et son attractivité auprès des Français. Cette dynamique illustre son rôle majeur dans leur épargne de long terme, mais aussi dans le financement de l’économie. Préserver pleinement cette contribution essentielle au financement de l’économie française et européenne constitue un enjeu majeur. » Pour en savoir plus sur l’assurance vie, cliquez ici. NB : l’arrondi d’un total ou d’une différence n’est pas nécessairement égal à la somme ou à la différence des arrondis de ses composantes. C’est parfois le cas entre la collecte nette d’une part et la différence entre les cotisations et les prestations d’autre part, lorsque ces grandeurs sont toutes trois arrondies en milliards d’euros. items.extracted_text: Avec 19,3 milliards d’euros de cotisations en juin 2026, les épargnants maintiennent leur confiance dans l’assurance vie - France Assureurs En juin 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 19,3 milliards d’euros, en forte progression de +12 % par rapport au même mois de 2025. À 12,6 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois de juin 2026 sont en hausse de +7 % par rapport à juin 2025. La collecte nette s’établit à +6,7 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +1,3 milliards d’euros par rapport à celle de juin 2025. À 19,3 milliards d’euros, les cotisations atteignent un nouveau record pour un mois de juin En juin 2026, les cotisations en assurance vie s’élèvent à 19,3 milliards d’euros, en forte progression de + 12 % par rapport au même mois de 2025. Elles établissent ainsi un nouveau record pour un mois de juin. Le plus haut niveau précédent remonte à juin 2025, avec 17,2 milliards d’euros de cotisations. Les cotisations progressent à un rythme plus soutenu pour les supports en unités de compte (UC, +15 %) que pour ceux en euros (+10 %). Depuis le début de l’année, les cotisations atteignent 108,8 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +10,1 milliards d’euros, soit +10 % par rapport aux six premiers mois de 2025. Cette progression concerne à la fois les supports en UC (+12 %) et ceux en euros (+9 %). La part des UC dans les cotisations s’établit à 43 % sur le mois de juin 2026 et à 39 % sur la première moitié de l’année. À 12,6 milliards d’euros, les prestations du mois de juin 2026 sont en hausse de +7 % par rapport à juin 2025. Cette augmentation est davantage portée par les supports en UC (+17 %) que par ceux en euros (−4 %). Depuis le début de l’année, les prestations s’élèvent à 72,3 milliards d’euros, en légère progression de +1,2 milliard d’euros, soit +2 % par rapport aux six premiers mois de 2025. La dynamique concerne essentiellement les supports en UC (+1,3 milliard d’euros, soit + 9 %), tandis que les prestations des supports en euros restent stables. La collecte nette s’établit donc à +6,7 milliards d’euros, en hausse de +1,3 milliards d’euros par rapport à celle du même mois de l’année précédente. Cette collecte nette positive concerne principalement les supports en UC (+5,4 milliards d’euros) et dans une moindre mesure ceux en euros (+1,3 milliards d’euros). Depuis le début de l’année, la collecte nette s’élève à +36,5 milliards d’euros, supérieure de +8,9 milliards d’euros à celle de 2025 sur la même période. La collecte nette au premier semestre 2026 atteint ainsi un plus haut niveau depuis le premier semestre 2006, où elle culminait à 40,2 milliards d’euros. Cette dynamique est portée par les supports en UC (+27,5 milliards d’euros), tandis que ceux en euros progressent de manière moins prononcée (+8,9 milliards d’euros). L’encours des contrats d’assurance vie atteint 2 162 milliards d’euros à fin juin 2026, en hausse de +6 % sur un an (+122 milliards d’euros). Au deuxième trimestre 2026, les cotisations sur les PER assurantiels sont en hausse de +8 % Au deuxième trimestre 2026, les cotisations (hors transferts) sur les PER assurantiels s’élèvent à 3,2 milliards d’euros, soit +8 % par rapport à la même période en 2025, pour 229 600 nouveaux PER souscrits. La collecte nette atteint +1,9 milliard d’euros, stable par rapport à la même période de 2025. Depuis le début de l’année 2026, les versements sur les PER assurantiels (y compris les transferts) s’élèvent à 9,4 milliards d’euros, en progression de + 2 % par rapport à la même période en 2025. Les transferts d’anciens contrats d’épargne retraite vers les PER ont représenté 52 200 assurés pour un montant de 1,6 milliard d’euros au deuxième trimestre 2026. À fin juin 2026, les PER assurantiels comptabilisent 8,5 millions d’assurés pour un encours de 124,8 milliards d’euros. Les entreprises d’assurance représentaient 70 % de l’encours de l’ensemble des PER à fin décembre 2025. Selon Paul ESMEIN, directeur général de France Assureurs : « Avec 19,3 milliards de cotisations en juin 2026, les Français confirment une nouvelle fois leur attachement à l’assurance vie. Cette dynamique, conjuguée au développement des PER assurantiels, est un bon signal : elle permet de répondre aux besoins des Français d’épargner sur le long terme, tout en contribuant au financement de l’économie française et européenne. Concrètement, à fin décembre 2025, 64 % des encours étaient en effet investis en titres d’entreprises et 24 % en obligations souveraines. » Pour en savoir plus sur l’assurance vie, cliquez ici. NB : l’arrondi d’un total ou d’une différence n’est pas nécessairement égal à la somme ou à la différence des arrondis de ses composantes. C’est parfois le cas entre la collecte nette d’une part et la différence entre les cotisations et les prestations d’autre part, lorsque ces grandeurs sont toutes trois arrondies en milliards d’euros. Les assureurs tiennent à exprimer leur soutien à toutes les personnes qui ont perdu leur habitation, leurs biens ou leur outil […] L’article Incendies en Gironde, dans les Landes et dans le Var : les assureurs expriment leur solidarité avec les sinistrés et annoncent des mesures exceptionnelles est apparu en premier sur France Assureurs .
items.extracted_text: Incendies en Gironde, dans les Landes et dans le Var : les assureurs expriment leur solidarité avec les sinistrés et annoncent des mesures exceptionnelles - France Assureurs La Gironde, les Landes et le Var affrontent actuellement des incendies de grande ampleur qui ont entraîné la destruction totale ou partielle de centaines de bâtiments et l’évacuation de centaines de milliers de personnes. Les assureurs tiennent à exprimer leur soutien à toutes les personnes qui ont perdu leur habitation, leurs biens ou leur outil de travail, ainsi qu’aux habitants contraints de quitter leur domicile, qui vivent aujourd’hui dans l’incertitude. Ils saluent le courage et l’engagement remarquable des sapeurs-pompiers, des forces de sécurité, des services de secours, des collectivités, des associations et de l’ensemble des personnes mobilisées auprès des populations concernées. Dans cette situation particulièrement éprouvante, les assureurs sont pleinement mobilisés pour accompagner leurs assurés et annoncent deux mesures exceptionnelles : Le délai de déclaration de sinistre est prolongé jusqu’au 31 août Les occupants ayant dû évacuer leur résidence principale à la demande des autorités, qu’elle ait été endommagée ou non, se verront proposer le remboursement sur justificatif de leurs frais de relogement pour une période de trois semaines tant que l’accès à celle-ci demeure interdit. Depuis plusieurs jours la Gironde, les Landes et le Var sont confrontés à des incendies d’une ampleur exceptionnelle. Ces feux ont causé d’importantes destructions et contraint plusieurs centaines de milliers de personnes à quitter leur domicile ou leur lieu de séjour. Dans ce contexte, les assureurs se mobilisent pour accompagner leurs assurés touchés par ces incendies toujours en cours. Ils annoncent plusieurs mesures : Prolongation du délai de déclaration de sinistre jusqu’au 31 août , au-delà des cinq jours du délai réglementaire Remboursement sur fourniture de justificatif(s), dans les conditions et limites fixées par le contrat en cas de dommages, des frais de relogement pour les occupants ayant dû évacuer leur résidence principale à la demande des autorités publiques, qu’elle ait été endommagée ou non, pour une période maximale de trois semaines, dans la limite de la période d’interdiction d’accès à la résidence principale. Par ailleurs, les assureurs ont renforcé leurs équipes de gestion et demandé aux cabinets d’experts de s’organiser pour accélérer les visites d’expertise dès que les accès aux zones sinistrées sera à nouveau possible. Selon Florence Lustman, présidente de France Assureurs : « Les incendies d’une ampleur exceptionnelle en Gironde, dans les Landes et le Var ont entraîné l’évacuation de centaines de milliers d’habitants de la région, dont certains sont confrontés à un problème de relogement au moins temporaire. Au nom de l’ensemble des assureurs, je tiens à exprimer notre profonde solidarité et notre soutien à toutes les personnes brutalement arrachées à leur quotidien, qui ont parfois tout perdu ou qui vivent dans l’angoisse de ce qu’ils retrouveront à leur retour. Dans cette situation exceptionnelle, notre priorité est d’apporter des réponses rapides et concrètes. Les assureurs ont ainsi décidé de prolonger le délai de déclaration de sinistre jusqu’au 31 août, de rembourser les frais de relogement des assurés ayant dû évacuer leur résidence principale, et ce pour une période de trois semaines tant que l’accès à leur résidence reste interdit. Les assureurs resteront pleinement mobilisés, aux côtés des pouvoirs publics, pour accompagner les sinistrés dans la durée. » Documents à télécharger Communiqué de presse – Incendies en Gironde, dans
